The advocate's load-bearing claim is: latency-slo-admitter appears in the plugin catalog but is "consistently ABSENT from the active schedulingProfiles list that actually runs per request," therefore admission-shedding isn't part of the canonical deployment. I traced the actual wiring code one layer deeper than the advocate did (none of these three files appear in their evidence list):

1. pkg/epp/requestcontrol/request_control_config.go — `Config.AddPlugins(pluginObjects ...plugin.Plugin)` iterates every plugin object and does a bare Go type-assertion `plugin.(fwkrc.Admitter)`; any match is appended to `admissionPlugins`. This has nothing to do with schedulingProfiles membership.
2. cmd/epp/runner/runner.go:805 — `r.requestControlConfig.AddPlugins(handle.GetAllPlugins()...)`, called with ALL plugins instantiated from the top-level YAML `plugins:` catalog (via `loader.InstantiateAndConfigure(rawConfig, ...)`), independent of schedulingProfiles.

4. pkg/epp/framework/plugins/requestcontrol/admitter/latencyslo/plugin.go:44 — `var _ requestcontrol.Admitter = &LatencyAdmission{}` confirms `latency-slo-admitter` implements exactly this interface.

So `schedulingProfiles` wires the Scheduler's filter/scorer/producer/picker pipeline only — a separate subsystem from admission. It is not "the list that actually runs per request" for admission plugins; the advocate mischaracterized what that YAML section governs. Any plugin merely declared in the top-level `plugins:` catalog that implements `Admitter` gets wired into the live per-request admission path regardless of schedulingProfiles.

The same bundling is visible in the "predicted-latency-slo" well-known test fixture (line 346, same catalog).

This also undercuts the "248 and 249 are cleanly separable plugins, double-counting one fact against two entries" argument: in the canonical deployment the advocate cites, they are not independently togglable — enabling 248's technique enables 249's mechanism as a package.

finding.reasoning: The entry's own live question was: does ZDR silently disable the separately-confirmed prompt-caching saving (id 164)? This is now answered from both providers' current primary docs, and the answer is no in both cases, with one real nuance. Anthropic's data-retention table (platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/api-and-data-retention) lists 'Prompt caching' as ZDR-eligible with the detail: 'Your prompts and Claude's outputs are not stored. KV cache representations and cryptographic hashes are held in memory for the cache TTL and promptly deleted after expiry.' Caching is not disabled under Anthropic ZDR. OpenAI's prompt-caching guide is more specific about a real (but bounded) side effect: 'Organizations without Zero Data Retention enabled default to 24h. Organizations with Zero Data Retention enabled default to in_memory when prompt_cache_retention is not specified.' And from the your-data guide: 'When Zero Data Retention is not enabled for an organization, all queries use extended prompt caching for all supported models.' So OpenAI ZDR does not disable caching either — it changes the DEFAULT retention window from 24h to in_memory (shorter TTL, so caches expire faster if the caller never explicitly overrides prompt_cache_retention), which could lower realized cache-hit rate for infrequently-repeated prefixes but leaves the caching mechanism and its per-hit discount intact. The specific fear the entry raised is settled: ZDR is not a silent kill-switch on caching for either provider. That said, the verdict for the ZDR gate itself lands at CONTRACTUAL_ONLY rather than PASS_ABSOLUTE, unlike ids 129/130/134: ZDR is not a pre-contract artifact with zero request-schema surface — it is a live, request-time server-behavior promise ('your prompts and outputs are not stored', OpenAI's 'the store parameter will always be treated as false') about the same serving pipeline that answers the call, and we have no way to externally verify Anthropic's or OpenAI's internal storage systems actually behave as documented. That is exactly the evidentiary ceiling that already caps id 164 (cache_control) and id 11 (msglm) at CONTRACTUAL_ONLY — a documented promise about internal handling, not an externally checkable architectural fact.

confirmations.reasoning: Confirmed, not settled either direction. Re-fetched the sole source (dirac.run/posts/agentic-cache-cost-simulation, 2026-08-20) and it is exactly what the entry says: a client-side random-token simulator, not measured production logs. Verbatim: 'The chart below simulates the actual costs. Each turn appends 200-3000 random input tokens, the model responds with ~200 output + ~100 thinking tokens, and a cache hit is rolled probabilistically.' The underlying 10:1 cached:uncached price ratio is real (Anthropic's own pricing table puts cache-read at 0.1x base input, confirmed elsewhere in this register at entry 74), so the *mechanism* -- a compounding multiplier as more turns pay the uncached rate -- is genuine arithmetic on real prices. But the specific headline magnitude ('20% cache-hit drop doubles your bill') is an artifact of the simulator's own randomized-token-count assumption, not a measurement of any real agentic workload, and real agentic loops are typically far more structurally cacheable (stable system prompt + tool defs, incrementally-appended turns) than a model that rolls 200-3000 *random* tokens per turn -- so the simulated sensitivity could easily overstate or understate a real fleet's exposure. Worth flagging for context: the author (Max Trivedi) writes for Dirac, a competing coding-agent product that itself 'continuously displays the weighted averaged cache hit rates' as a feature -- this is vendor content with an interest in cache-hit-rate anxiety being a live concern, which doesn't make the arithmetic wrong but is a reason not to launder it as neutral data. No live-traffic access this sweep to run the correlation myself, so the entry stands as submitted: real ratio, simulated magnitude, diagnostic rather than technique.

confirmations.settlingExperiment: Sharper version of the entry's own experiment: pull cache_read_input_tokens / cache_creation_input_tokens / input_tokens from usage objects already sitting in real logs (Claude Code's own session transcripts under ~/.claude/projects/, or any customer's existing Helicone/Langfuse export) for ~20-30 real agentic sessions spanning a natural range of realized cache-hit rates -- no new API spend required, this is a log-mining exercise, a few hours. Compute actual $ cost per session from the real usage numbers and real per-provider pricing, then regress cost against realized cache-hit rate. Settles high (simulator's magnitude roughly holds) if the fitted marginal effect of a 20-point cache-hit-rate drop lands within ~1.5x-3x total-cost increase; settles low (simulator overstates real exposure) if real agentic loops cluster tightly near 90%+ hit rate regardless of turn count -- because real prefixes are structurally stable, not randomly regenerated -- making the simulated sensitivity a worst-case bound nobody's real traffic actually hits.

'claude_code:'+rec.requestId when present/non-empty; else 'syn:'+sha256 of [source,accountId,projectId,ts,model,inputTokens,cacheReadTokens,cacheCreationTokens,outputTokens]. Synthesized-key dedup is only as strong as that 8-field tuple — two distinct requests with identical ts+model+all four token totals collide silently and get counted as deduped, not as data loss.
opts.accountId, defaulting to constant 'local'. Not read from the record — transcripts carry no billing-account id at all.
opts.projectId, caller-supplied (CLI derives it from the transcript directory name). Not read from the record itself.
rec.timestamp verbatim — the assistant record's wall-clock instant. One instant per request; no start/end pair.

Constant 'claude_code'.
rec.message.usage.service_tier if it matches one of the 6 known tier strings, else null.
rec.message.model, required string.

Summed across usage.iterations[] when present (each iteration's own usage-shaped fields), else read straight off the top-level usage object. Iterations path exists because Anthropic bills the sum of usage.iterations, not the top level, when compaction fires — a top-level-only reader under-reports by up to 8.6x on their documented example.

From usage.cache_creation.ephemeral_{5m,1h}_input_tokens when either key is present; otherwise the whole cache_creation_input_tokens total is dumped into the 5m bucket (the cheaper of the two rates, so this can only under-state cost, never over-state it) and the shortfall is counted in provenance.unknownTtlWrites.
Sum of every iteration whose type !== 'message' (coded generically, not literally gated on type==='compaction'). Zero for any request that didn't compact.

Filters to only 'assistant' records; anything else (user turns, tool-result turns, summaries, unknown types) is dropped and counted as skippedNonAssistant, with no per-type breakdown of what was skipped.

Never read at all — explicit design point, verified by a canary-string test ('no prompt content survives the import'). No content, no content length, no content structure of any kind reaches an event.

Checked only for presence/object-type to increment provenance.thinkingDetailRecords (a count of records that HAD the field). The actual thinking-vs-visible-output token split inside it is never read into the event.
Used only to route counts into total vs. compaction buckets; the number of iterations, their individual types/sizes, or ordering is not preserved past that binary split.

signals.field: linesSeen, imported, malformed, deduped, synthesizedKeys, skippedNonAssistant, compactionEvents, unknownTtlWrites, hiddenInputTokens, hiddenOutputTokens, thinkingDetailRecords

Several of these fields exist ONLY to make the hash collision-safe — they are never copied onto the resulting event.
r.account_id, else opts.accountFallback, else constant 'org'.
r.workspace_id, else constant 'default' — the cost-centre axis for this source is the workspace, not the account.
bucket.starting_at only — the START of an aggregation window, not a per-request timestamp. Could represent a 1-minute, 1-hour, or 1-day bucket; the event carries no signal of which.
Hardcoded null. Doc comment: 'Aggregate buckets have no session. Anything session-shaped must decline to run.'
Constant 'admin_usage_report'.
r.service_tier if one of the 6 known strings, else null.
r.model, required non-empty string.
r.uncached_input_tokens — a differently-named field than the claudeCode source's input_tokens, but mapped to the same schema slot.
r.cache_read_input_tokens.
r.output_tokens.

r.cache_creation.ephemeral_5m_input_tokens / ephemeral_1h_input_tokens, defaulting to 0 each — this source always reports the exact split (no 'unknown TTL, assume cheap' fallback exists here, unlike claudeCode).
Computed as the sum of the two TTL buckets above — there is no separate combined field consumed for this source.

Hardcoded 0, always. Compaction cost IS folded into this source's totals upstream (unlike claudeCode where it's broken out) but is structurally invisible as a separate line item — comment: 'claiming a share here would be inventing one.'
Read only as a hash input for key uniqueness across adjacent buckets; never becomes part of the event, so bucket width/granularity is unrecoverable downstream.
Read only for the idempotency hash. Per-API-key spend attribution is impossible after import despite the source providing it.
Same fate — hash input only, discarded before the event exists.
e.g. '0-200k' in the fixture; hash-only. Doc comment lists it among 'what the levers need' but the code never surfaces it on an event.

The fast-mode-2026-02-01 beta flag; hash-only. A 'did fast mode save money' lever has nothing to query for this after import.

Present in the test fixture representing the real Admin API result shape, but never read by any line of import code — confirmed by repo-wide grep returning zero hits for server_tool_use/web_search/code_execution anywhere in src/. Server-side tool billing is invisible to the whole pipeline, not merely dropped after reading.

signals.field: pages, buckets, results, imported, malformed, deduped, unpriceableTier
signals.meaning: Aggregate counters for one import call. unpriceableTier flags non-standard/non-batch tiers that costOfEvent will later refuse, but only as a count, not as a list of which model/window combinations.

signals.field: Totals{events, microCents, inputTokens, cacheReadTokens, cacheCreationTokens, cacheCreation5mTokens, cacheCreation1hTokens, outputTokens}
signals.meaning: Per-scope sums (overall/byModel/byProject/byAccount) computed once costOfEvent succeeds. This is the finest-grained aggregate a lever gets for free; anything below it (per-event, per-session) requires walking events[] directly.
cacheReadTokens / (cacheReadTokens + inputTokens). Cache WRITE volume is structurally excluded from the denominator by design — this ratio cannot answer 'what fraction of writes ever got read back'.
Pricing-coverage gap counts — how many imported events computeMetrics had to exclude from cost, by reason.
Sorted, deduped list of model ids missing from the active rate card — a report-actionable signal, not just a count.

Sorted, deduped list of UsageEvent.source values that actually contributed priced events — computed from the events themselves, not inferred from which maps are populated (explicitly fixed after a prior bug where it was guessed).

Cache-write tokens as an integer % of cache-eligible input, or null with no eligible input. A single batch-average proxy for 'how much am I paying to write cache' — cannot localize which specific writes were wasteful.

A 5-value ranked enum (PASS_ABSOLUTE, PASS_METADATA, PASS_SCHEDULING, PASS_REPLAY, CONTRACTUAL_ONLY) classifying how a proposed savings FINDING is proven, independent of any UsageEvent field. isProvable() is true only for PASS_ABSOLUTE/PASS_REPLAY (demonstrable without trusting provider prose); shipsByDefault() is false only for CONTRACTUAL_ONLY (moves execution to a different fleet, so byte-identity can't be proven even in principle). Nothing in the importers or metrics computes this automatically — it's declared per-lever by whoever writes the finding.

absent: Retry/attempt markers: no field anywhere distinguishes a first attempt from a retry after timeout/error/rate-limit, and there is no attempt count — a 'stop retrying so much' lever has nothing to detect retries with.
Error/failure status: no is_error, stop_reason, or refusal flag on either source. A request that consumed full input+output tokens and then failed/refused is indistinguishable from a successful one.

Wall-clock duration / latency / time-to-first-token: ts is a single instant (assistant-record timestamp for claudeCode; bucket START only for admin). There is no end time, no per-request duration, anywhere.

Prompt/response content: deliberately never carried past the parsed line, by design and by test (canary-string assertions in both importer test suites). No content, length, or structure of any message reaches an event — a lever cannot see whether the cached prefix is boilerplate, unique, or shortenable.

Cache breakpoint count/location (cache_control placement): only aggregate written/read TOTALS per event; no signal for how many breakpoints were set, where in the conversation, or whether the 4-breakpoint API limit was exceeded.

Cache-entry recency/age at read time: cacheReadTokens is a bare count with no link to which prior write it read back or how close to TTL expiry that read landed. Explicitly documented as impossible for admin_usage_report: 'There are no timestamps per call and no session, so anything that needs the gap between consecutive turns — TTL right-sizing above all — cannot be computed from this source.'

Server-side tool-use billing (web_search_requests, code_execution, etc.): present in the real Admin API payload shape (per the test fixture's server_tool_use field) but read by zero lines of code anywhere in src/. Tool-use spend is entirely invisible to this pipeline, not just dropped after reading.

Per-API-key / per-service-account attribution: api_key_id and service_account_id are read by adminUsageReport ONLY to seed the idempotency hash, then discarded — spend cannot be sliced by key or service account after import despite the raw source providing both.

context_window, inference_geo, speed (admin fast-mode beta): same fate — consumed only for hash uniqueness, never copied onto UsageEvent. A lever asking 'did fast-mode cost less' or 'which region did this run in' has nothing to query post-import even though the module's own doc comment names these as things 'the levers need.'

Bucket window width (admin source): UsageEvent.ts carries only bucket.starting_at; ending_at is hash-only. The aggregation granularity (1m vs 1h vs 1d) of any admin event is unrecoverable from the event itself.

Extended-thinking token split: usage.output_tokens_details is checked only for presence, incrementing a batch counter (thinkingDetailRecords); the actual thinking-vs-visible-output split is never read into any token field. Measured (per code comment) at 0 of 108,042 real records carrying the field at all.

Conversation/session structure beyond a bare sessionId: no parentUuid/message-chain linkage, no turn index, no isSidechain or subagent marker, no conversation length. Cannot separate primary-flow cost from subagent/sidechain cost, or compute cost per logical task within a session.
Actor/human identity: no user id or userType (human- vs. agent-initiated) on either source. Spend cannot be attributed to a specific operator.

Repo/branch/working-directory context: projectId is only a caller-supplied label (transcript directory name for claudeCode; workspace_id for admin) — no cwd, git branch, or repo identity is ever read from the transcript content itself.

Model pin vs. moving alias: model is a bare string with no flag for whether a dated snapshot or a floating alias was requested — a 'pin models so pricing/behavior can't shift under you' lever has no signal to check.
Rate-limit / throttling signals (429s, backoff, queue depth, concurrency at request time): absent entirely from both sources.
Batch job/submission id: service_tier can say 'batch', but there is no batch job id anywhere, so batch-tier spend cannot be tied back to a specific submitted job for batch-usage right-sizing.

Request/message structural size: no signal for number of turns, number of tool definitions, system-prompt size, or number of distinct content blocks — only aggregate token totals, so nothing distinguishes 'oversized system prompt every call' from 'oversized conversation history.'

Iteration-level detail on compaction (claudeCode only): all non-'message' iteration types collapse into one compactionInputTokens/OutputTokens pair per event; the count of iterations, their individual sizes, or any type other than the observed 'compaction' are not individually preserved.

A message-level API identifier distinct from the transcript's requestId (e.g. a response 'id: msg_...' field): claudeCode reads only rec.requestId; no separate response-message id is captured, so cross-referencing an event against a raw API response log by its own id is not possible.

levers.name: Cache-hit headroom (Anthropic prompt-cache read discount) — existing lever
requiredSignals: metrics.byModel Totals: inputTokens, cacheReadTokens (already computed by computeMetrics)
operator-set targetCacheHitPct (existing Assumptions field)
operator-set cacheWriteOverheadPct, default 5 (existing Assumptions field, spec §6.7)
RateCard.cacheRead / cacheWrite / cacheWrite1h per model (rates.ts)
levers.formulaSketch: Exactly simulate.ts's priceBundle(): eligible = inputTokens + cacheReadTokens; read = floor(eligible*targetCacheHitPct/100); fresh = eligible-read; written = floor(eligible*cacheWriteOverheadPct/100) routed entirely into cacheCreation5mTokens (simulated writes always price at the cheaper 5m regime, never 1h); price via costOfEvent per model, sum over metrics.byModel; savedMicroCents = baseline - simulated.
levers.honestyNotes: Already implemented and already honest: target==observed floors to $0 (AC5), and the ids in this group (litellm/langchain wrappers ids 9,10; the raw cache_control mechanics ids 60,68,74,136,164; the usage-object measurement primitive id29; TTL/retention framing ids 84,141,147,163,167,168; the msglm wrapper id11) all price through the *same* 0.1x-read/1.25x-1h-write mechanism this formula already uses — they add corroboration, not new math. The one place this could flatter a number: cacheWriteOverheadPct too low understates the cost of reaching the simulated hit rate. Default 5% is a documented assumption, not a measurement — must stay operator-overridable and never silently tuned down to inflate savedMicroCents.

levers.name: TTL right-sizing recovery (1h cache write bought, 5m would have sufficed)
requiredSignals: UsageEvent.sessionId (non-null) — present for claude_code source, absent for admin_usage_report aggregates
UsageEvent.ts per event
UsageEvent.cacheCreation1hTokens
RateCard.cacheWrite vs cacheWrite1h per model
levers.formulaSketch: Exactly src/detect/ttlRightSizing.ts, already built: group events by sessionId, sort by ts; for each event e with e.cacheCreation1hTokens>0, find next event in the same session; if next exists and gap = Date.parse(next.ts)-Date.parse(e.ts) is finite and <= FIVE_MINUTES_MS, overBoughtTokens += e.cacheCreation1hTokens and recoverableMicroCents += e.cacheCreation1hTokens * (card.rates[e.model].cacheWrite1h - card.rates[e.model].cacheWrite). This needs zero operator input — it is pure transcript/admin-report metadata (session + timestamp + model + the 1h/5m split already carried on every UsageEvent) — but its output is never surfaced through simulate.ts's Simulation type. Wiring detectTtlRightSizing's recoverableMicroCents into a new Simulation.ttlRightSizing field is the only gap; no new formula is needed.
levers.honestyNotes: The detector is already deliberately conservative in ways that must survive the wiring: (1) computable=false (aggregate admin_usage_report data with no sessionId) must report UNQUANTIFIED, never $0 — a whole-input-without-sessions is the wrong instrument for the question, per the detector's own docstring. (2) neverReReadTokens (last event in a session, or a write that's never re-read at all) is counted separately and explicitly claimed as nothing — folding it into this lever's recoverable figure would double-count the day a waste/duplicate detector (the register's Family E, already UNQUANTIFIED in simulate.ts) lands. (3) The detector does not model the miss penalty of actually shortening a TTL (a prefix re-read between 5min and 1h would then pay a fresh write instead of a 0.1x read) — on the measured sample this is ~1% of write volume, but the function has no way to know that on a different traffic shape, so the recovered figure is a floor, not a guaranteed net.

levers.name: Batch API tier (opt-in 50% off, Anthropic Message Batches)
requiredSignals: operator-set targetBatchPct — new Assumptions field, same shape as targetCacheHitPct
UsageEvent.source, to exclude claude_code interactive sessions from eligibility (batch has ~24h turnaround)
pricing.ts TIER_MULTIPLIER.batch = 0.5 (already implemented, unused by simulate.ts today)
levers.formulaSketch: New code, same shape as priceBundle's cacheTargetPct branch, on a second independent axis: given operator-set targetBatchPct, batched = scale(bundle, targetBatchPct) priced through costOfEvent with serviceTier='batch' applied across inputTokens, cacheReadTokens, cacheCreation5mTokens, cacheCreation1hTokens, outputTokens; sync = scale(bundle, 100-targetBatchPct) priced as observed (serviceTier=null/standard); savedMicroCents = baseline - (batched+sync). No new pricing math — TIER_MULTIPLIER.batch already exists in pricing.ts, this only needs a second scale()+tier call alongside the existing cache-target one.
levers.honestyNotes: This is the register's clearest 'contractual entry worth an opt-in lever' (task's own example). It must default to targetBatchPct=0 (⇒ $0 saved) absent an explicit operator input, matching the '=observed⇒$0' precedent — Claude Code transcripts carry zero signal that any given request is latency-tolerant enough for a ~24h turnaround (batch has no tool-calling on some transports either), so eligibility can never be inferred, only declared. Two id-181-adjacent facts keep the formula honest without a separate lever: errored/canceled/expired batch requests bill at $0 (id 181, folded into L13 below), so this formula must NOT subtract an estimated failure-rate cost — that would understate the saving; and ids 261/263 describe how one might build an actual auto-batching router, which token-spread does not do — it only estimates a recommendation, so the honestyNotes must say this lever prices a hypothetical operator decision, not a behavior change token-spread performs. If this and the cache-headroom lever (L1) are ever combined, the combined figure must reprice the same bundle through BOTH tier and cache-target simultaneously (product), never sum the two levers' independently-computed savings — per simulate.ts's existing 'combined = product, never sum' rule.

levers.name: Cache-configuration hygiene diagnostics (precursor checks for L1)
requiredSignals: model id + measured cacheCreationTokens by model, cross-referenced against each model's known minimum-cacheable-prefix floor (id26, computable today from existing byModel Totals)
count of content/cache_control blocks since the last breakpoint per request — NOT available; UsageEvent carries only aggregated token totals, no per-block structure (id165)
framework/SDK identifier per account/session — NOT available (id25, id175)
levers.formulaSketch: N/A — these are structural presence/absence checks, not token-count formulas. id26 is partially computable today (cacheCreationTokens==0 despite input tokens exceeding a model's documented floor is a real byModel-level signature); ids 165/25/175 need request-shape or framework metadata this product's content-blind UsageEvent schema does not carry.
levers.honestyNotes: These would explain WHY an account's observed cache-hit rate undershoots what L1's simulation assumes achievable, but the dollar impact of a fixed misconfiguration is already fully captured by L1's own gap between observed and simulated hit rate — pricing these separately would double-count the same missing cache reads L1 already prices. Report as warnings only ('cache_creation==0 on a Haiku prefix that should clear the floor'), never as an incremental $ figure.

levers.name: TTL forced-miss on subscription→usage-credit billing crossing
requiredSignals: billing-pool/regime per event (subscription-drawdown vs usage-credit) — NOT present in UsageEvent today
idle-gap length per session — available (ts, sessionId already carried)

contract.contract:
INTEGRATION CONTRACT — adding a new savings lever to token-spread
(research only; nothing in the repo was edited to produce this)

## 1. The pipeline a lever must join

    events[] -> computeMetrics() -> simulate()/detect*() -> buildReport() -> renderAuditHtml() -> cli.ts flags
                (src/metrics.ts)   (src/simulate.ts or     (src/report.ts)  (src/render/auditHtml.ts) (src/cli.ts)
                                    src/detect/<lever>.ts)

There are exactly two shapes a lever can take, both already exemplified in the codebase:

  A. A SIMULATION lever (parametric "what if X% -> Y%") — lives inside src/simulate.ts,
     alongside cache-hit headroom. It takes an operator-set Assumption, re-prices a token
     `Bundle` through `priceBundle()`, and its output rides `Simulation.cacheHeadroom`-shaped
     fields or a sibling of it.
  B. A DETECTOR/FINDING lever (measured directly from events, no operator knob) — lives in its
     own file under src/detect/<name>.ts, mirroring src/detect/ttlRightSizing.ts exactly:
     export a `detect<Name>(events, card): <Name>Finding` that is pure, takes events + RateCard,
     returns a finding object with `evidence`, a computability flag, and `*MicroCents`. This is
     the template to copy for a second finding — it is the only other lever the codebase has.

Both shapes converge on `Report.findings[]` (detector levers) or `Report.savings`/`cacheHeadroom`
(simulation levers), and both must be threaded through buildReport()'s input object, which is
itself threaded through cli.ts's five call sites (build the input, decide flags, refuse-on-empty
checks, humanSummary, JSON/-html output).

## 2. Every file a new lever must touch

Core pipeline (required for any lever):
  - src/detect/<lever>.ts (NEW, detector shape) — pure function, `export interface <Lever>Finding`,
    doc comment stating what it does NOT model (ttlRightSizing.ts's precedent: state the
    unmodeled miss-penalty case explicitly, in prose, in the file).
    OR: extend src/simulate.ts's `Assumptions`/`Simulation` interfaces + `priceBundle`/`totalCost`
    for a simulation-shape lever.
  - src/report.ts — thread the new input through `buildReport()`'s parameter object; add to
    `Report.findings[]` (if detector-shaped) or a new named field beside `cacheHeadroom` (if
    simulation-shaped); extend `savings.allMeasured` arithmetic (see AC floor below — this is
    the single highest-risk edit); add a line to `humanSummary`; add an `AssumptionNote` if the
    lever has an operator-set knob.
  - src/render/auditHtml.ts — add a `.lever` block (detector findings render automatically via
    `r.findings.map(...)` if the lever populates `findings[]`; a simulation-shaped lever needs
    its own explicit block, following the `r.savings.cacheOnly.cents > 0 ? ... : ""` pattern).
    Anything customer-supplied MUST go through `esc()`.
  - src/cli.ts — if the lever takes an operator-set assumption, add a `--flag` to the `FLAGS`
    array (this single array is both `--help` text and the unknown-flag validator — one list,
    cannot disagree), read it with `arg()`/`flag()`, thread it into the `buildReport()` call and
    into `assumptions`. Every field the lever adds to a shared counter object (e.g. provenance-
    style objects) must be listed at BOTH its point of initialization in cli.ts AND accumulated
    in the `for (const k of Object.keys(...))` merge loop — a field present in the type but
    absent from the literal is silently never accumulated (this is the exact class of bug
    thinkingDetailRecords hit on 2026-08-12, and tests/cliContract.test.ts now greps cli.ts's
    source for every provenance key by name specifically to catch it again).

Type/pricing layer (touch only if the lever needs new token categories or a new evidence class):
  - src/types.ts — UsageEvent, if the lever needs a token category `costOfEvent` doesn't already
    carry (e.g. TTL right-sizing needed the 5m/1h split added here). `USAGE_EVENT_KEYS` must
    also gain the new key.
  - src/pricing.ts — `costOfEvent()` ONLY if a genuinely new rate dimension is being priced
    (new tier multiplier, new token category). This is "the single pricing function" — simulate.ts
    and any new lever MUST call it, never re-derive gross = tokens*rate by hand.
  - src/evidence.ts — only if the lever's identity claim doesn't fit the five existing
    EVIDENCE_CLASSES (PASS_ABSOLUTE/PASS_METADATA/PASS_SCHEDULING/PASS_REPLAY/CONTRACTUAL_ONLY).
    In practice a new lever should be able to pick an existing class; adding a sixth is a
    register-level decision, not a lever-level one.

Tests (see section 4 for the exact patterns to copy):
  - tests/<lever>.test.ts — unit tests on the pure detector/simulate function, fixture-style,
    following ttlRightSizing.test.ts or simulate.test.ts line for line.
  - tests/report.test.ts — extend or add assertions that the lever's figure reaches buildReport()
    output and is tagged measured/operator_set correctly.
  - tests/auditHtml.test.ts — extend or add assertions that the lever's HTML block renders,
    escapes customer strings, and states unmeasurable cases as exposure rather than omitting them.
  - tests/recoverable.test.ts (acceptance.test.ts is the actual filename) — the disjointness test
    here (`the disjointness assumption behind adding rather than compounding still holds`) is
    DESIGNED to fail the moment `r.findings` contains a lever name other than
    "cache-write TTL right-sizing". That failure is not a bug to route around — it is the gate
    telling you to change `savings.allMeasured`'s arithmetic from addition to a compounding
    formula, per the AC floor below. Update that test's `levers` allowlist deliberately once you
    have made the arithmetic decision, not before.

Documentation/generated artifacts (see section 5 — this is where the site/ handoff lives):
  - docs/specs/2026-08-08-savings-report-design.md — §11.1's "Assumption register" table should
    gain a row if the lever retires an assumption from operator-set to measured. NOTE this spec
    is already stale in one place: AC4 ("Routing identity") describes a routing lever that was
    subsequently ripped out by design (simulate.ts / simulate.test.ts's "identity bar" tests
    assert `routingCurve` must NOT exist) — don't resurrect it as a template, and don't be
    surprised the spec doesn't match code 1:1 everywhere.
  - README.md, RUNNING.md — update the flags table and examples if a CLI flag was added.

## 3. AC floors the existing code enforces (a new lever inherits every one of these; none is optional)

  1. TARGET = OBSERVED PRICES TO EXACTLY $0. Spec AC5 / simulate.ts's explicit comment: a
     simulated regime whose target equals the already-observed state must be treated as "no
     lever applied" and priced identically to the null case — never run through the
     synthesized-volume path, which would charge phantom cost. simulate.test.ts pins this with
     TWO tests (zero observed rate, and nonzero observed rate) plus a THIRD test added
     specifically because the first two used a zero-cache-write fixture that couldn't see a
     related phantom (repricing observed 1h writes at the cheaper 5m rate and calling the
     difference a saving). Any new simulation-shaped lever with an analogous "target == current
     state" case must have this same three-part test: zero case, nonzero case, and a fixture
     that has pre-existing non-baseline state in the dimension the lever touches.
  2. UNQUANTIFIED IS A DISTINCT VALUE FROM $0. `export const UNQUANTIFIED = "UNQUANTIFIED"` — a
     lever with no signal in the current data reports this literal, typed `Unquantified`, never
     `0`. Reporting 0 reads as "measured, found nothing"; UNQUANTIFIED reads as "not measured
     here." `wasteOnly` in Simulation.attribution is the existing example. A new lever that
     sometimes cannot be computed (see ttlRightSizing's `computable: false` for aggregate-source
     admin reports, which have no session/timestamp) must expose the same distinction — either an
     UNQUANTIFIED sentinel or an explicit boolean `computable` flag that the report and HTML
     render as "exposure, not a saving" (see auditHtml.ts's `.warn` block for `!r.ttlRightSizing.
     computable && exposedTokens > 0`).
  3. INTEGER MICRO-CENTS EVERYWHERE, FLOORED ONCE. pricing.ts's `costOfEvent` computes gross
     as a float-free integer expression and floors exactly once at the very end
     (`Math.floor(gross * tier)`) — never per token category. `microCentsToCents()` (half-up) is
     the ONLY place micro-cents become cents, called once at the report boundary, never per
     event. A new lever must never introduce its own rounding step mid-pipeline; accumulate in
     microCents, convert once.
  4. ONE PRICING FUNCTION. `costOfEvent()` in pricing.ts is called by both `computeMetrics()` and
     `simulate.ts`'s `priceBundle()` (via a synthetic UsageEvent with `idempotencyKey: ""` that
     is never emitted/stored) — the doc comment is explicit: "if the report and the invoice ever
     disagree, the product is dead." A new lever must price through `costOfEvent`, never write a
     second copy of `tokens * rate`.
  5. LEVERS COMPOUND (MULTIPLY), NEVER ADD — UNLESS PROVABLY DISJOINT TOKEN CLASSES. Spec AC6.
     The one exception implemented today (cache-hit headroom + TTL right-sizing summed in
     `savings.allMeasured`) is only correct because the two levers touch disjoint token
     categories (fresh input vs. cache writes) — report.ts's comment on `allMeasured` and
     acceptance.test.ts's pinned "disjointness" test both say so explicitly, and that test is
     designed to break the instant a new finding's lever name appears, forcing a conscious
     decision: either prove new-lever-disjoint-from-existing-levers and extend the sum, or
     rewrite `allMeasured` as a compounding formula. A new lever CANNOT be silently added into
     the sum without addressing this test.
  6. NO ROUTING LEVER, EVER. simulate.ts's "identity bar" section and its dedicated tests
     (`simulate exposes no routing lever`, `assumptions carry no routing knobs`) exist
     specifically to keep a routing/model-switching lever from reappearing — "a different model
     answering is a different answer" and fails the product's core identity guarantee. A new
     lever must be provable same-model/same-output (an EvidenceClass from evidence.ts), never a
     "route to a cheaper model" mechanism.
  7. HEADLINE FIGURE CANNOT BE BELOW ANY FINDING IT CLAIMS TO CONTAIN. acceptance.test.ts's
     first test is a property test over this: `savings.allMeasured.cents >=` every
     `finding.saved.cents`, for whatever the traffic produces — this is the regression test for
     the exact bug that shipped ($0.00 headline over a $374.93 finding). A new lever must not be
     able to make the headline read lower than itself.
  8. EVERY SKIP/EXCLUSION REASON HAS A VOICE — NO SILENT $0. report.ts's warnings section: three
     `metrics.skipped` reasons (unknown_model, unknown_tier, malformed) each produce their own
     warning; cli.ts refuses (exit 1) both on zero events imported AND on events-imported-but-
     zero-priced. A new lever that can silently exclude events from its own denominator must warn
     about it the same way, not just leave it out of the count.
  9. NO NEW DEPENDENCY, NO NEW SOCKET. RUNNING.md/tests/cliContract.test.ts assert the local
     importer completes with `fetch` stubbed to throw. A lever must stay pure (events + RateCard
     in, finding out) — no I/O inside src/detect/ or src/simulate.ts.
 10. DETERMINISM. report.test.ts and auditHtml.test.ts both assert byte-identical / JSON-identical
     output across repeated runs on the same input. A new lever must not read the clock, Math.random,
     or object-iteration order that Node/Bun doesn't guarantee (report.ts already guards this with
     `.sort()` on every `Object.entries` it renders).
 11. CUSTOMER-SUPPLIED STRINGS ARE ESCAPED. Any lever detail/evidence string interpolated into
     auditHtml.ts's template must go through `esc()` — auditHtml.test.ts has a dedicated XSS test.

## 4. Test patterns actually used (no golden-file framework, no snapshot testing, no property-testing library)

  - HAND-COMPUTED FIXTURES, NOT SNAPSHOTS. Every dollar figure in a test is asserted against a
    value computed by hand in a comment (e.g. simulate.test.ts: "100 MTok fresh input... ->
    $750.00 baseline", "opus-5: 1h write 1000 micro-cents/token, 5m write 625 -> 375 recoverable
    per token"). Spec §10 states the rule explicitly: "checked against a different instrument
    than the code that produces the number (never assert the cost function against itself)."
    Copy this: write the lever's expected saving by hand, in the test file, before running code.
  - IN-MEMORY EVENT BUILDERS OVER FILE FIXTURES FOR UNIT TESTS. ttlRightSizing.test.ts and
    simulate.test.ts construct `UsageEvent[]` literals inline (a small `ev()`/literal-object
    helper) rather than reading fixtures/*.jsonl for most cases — fixtures/*.jsonl (mixed.jsonl,
    dupes.jsonl, malformed.jsonl, cache-ttl.jsonl, nokey.jsonl, compaction.jsonl) are reserved for
    importer-level and end-to-end report/auditHtml tests that need to exercise the whole import
    path. A new detector's unit tests should use inline builders; its report.ts/auditHtml.ts
    integration tests should reuse fixtures/mixed.jsonl or add a new fixtures/<lever>.jsonl only
    if the existing fixtures can't exercise it.
  - NEGATIVE/BOUNDARY TESTS ARE PAIRED WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL. Nearly every "X warns" test is
    immediately followed by "clean traffic does NOT warn" (report.test.ts's write-overhead-
    divergence test, unpriceable.test.ts's service-tier warning test). A lever's warning/finding
    logic needs both directions tested, not just the triggering case.
  - REGRESSION TESTS NAME THE BUG AND THE DATE IN A COMMENT, THEN ASSERT THE PROPERTY, NOT THE
    INCIDENT. acceptance.test.ts (Recoverable-tile bug) and unpriceable.test.ts ($0.00-over-
    priority-tier bug) both open with a paragraph: what broke, when it was found, who found it
    (adversarial review), and why the obvious fix ("just check this one case") isn't what got
    written — the fix is a general property (headline >= every finding; every skip reason warns)
    that also happens to cover the reported case, so a *different* future bug of the same shape
    fails the same test rather than needing a new one.
  - END-TO-END, THROUGH THE REAL CLI SUBPROCESS, FOR EXIT-CODE/STDERR CONTRACTS. cliContract.test.ts
    and unpriceable.test.ts spawn `bun run src/cli.ts` as a child process and assert on exit code
    + stderr text, not just on the exported functions — flag validation, missing-value handling,
    and the "no priceable events" refusal are contract-tested at the process boundary because
    that's the interface a user actually hits.
  - SOURCE-GREP TESTS FOR "TWO PLACES THAT MUST AGREE." cliContract.test.ts's last test literally
    reads cli.ts's source text and diffs it against `Object.keys(provenance)` from the type's
    runtime shape, to catch a field present in the type but silently unaccumulated in the CLI's
    merge loop. publishedTestCount.test.ts, publishedRates.test.ts, publishedCounts.test.ts do
    the same thing at repo scale (see section 5) — this codebase treats "prose about a number"
    and "the number" as two independent sources of truth that must be gated against each other,
    not narrated once and trusted.
  - NO MOCKING FRAMEWORK, NO GOLDEN IMAGE DIFFING IN THE TEST SUITE ITSELF. Visual/screenshot
    drift (section 5) is checked by separate .mjs scripts under site/tools/ and docs/media/,
    run manually via package.json scripts, NOT part of `bun run test`.

## 5. Where a new lever makes the audit-HTML screenshots/generated docs drift — DO NOT TOUCH, HANDOFF ONLY

site/ is a separately-deployed marketing site owned by another session (confirmed live right
now: `git status` on this checkout shows uncommitted changes to site/index.html,
site/index-scroll.html, site/methods.html, and README.md from in-flight work on branch
feat/register-sweep-13 — a different track entirely, about the 187-technique citation register,
not the savings-report levers). Any lever change to src/render/auditHtml.ts or src/report.ts's

     committed, and both PNGs stale one script-run after that. `bun run shoot:audit:check`
     exists precisely to detect this (byte-size delta >2% = drift, exit 1) but does not run in
     `bun run test` or in CI per package.json — it's manual.
     -> site/sample-audit.html is inside site/: DO NOT regenerate it from our session. Flag to
        the site-owning session: "auditHtml.ts changed shape; site/sample-audit.html and both
        derived PNGs need `shoot:audit` re-run."
  2. docs/img/savings-waterfall.png / .svg (README.md line 243, alt text literally states

     a nonzero finding on that exact worked example (e.g. a lever triggered by "nothing cached"

  3. Test-count cascade (publishedTestCount.test.ts): every lever adds tests, changing the total
     away from the currently-pinned 210. This is enforced by a SINGLE test that requires FOUR
     locations to agree exactly: README.md (badge + quickstart comment), RUNNING.md (quickstart

     will NOT make publishedTestCount.test.ts pass on its own, because site/BRIEF.md still says
     the old number. This is a hard cross-session blocking dependency, not a cosmetic drift — the
     test suite goes red until the other session's file is updated too.

        '**210 tests**' line (site/BRIEF.md, currently line 87) needs updating to N, or

     and site/BRIEF.md among its file list (confirmed: PAGES array includes both) — a new lever
     doesn't change rates, so this is lower risk, but if a lever's fixture/example touches a rate

Net: a new lever is fully buildable and testable (src/, tests/, docs/specs/, README.md,
RUNNING.md, docs/img/, bench/margin-model.ts) without ever writing into site/, but it CANNOT be
called fully "done" against the existing test suite without a handoff to whoever owns site/ for:
site/sample-audit.html + its two derived PNGs, and the test-count line in site/BRIEF.md (and,
conditionally, any rate/dollar-figure prose in site/BRIEF.md, site/index.html, site/pricing.html,
site/methods.html that cites the specific worked-example numbers). Surface that as an explicit
message to the site session rather than working around it (e.g. by skipping
publishedTestCount.test.ts) — skipping the gate defeats the reason it exists.
acFloors: Target = observed prices to exactly $0 (spec AC5) — a simulated regime whose target equals the already-observed state must short-circuit to the null-lever pricing path, never the synthesized-volume path; pinned by 3 tests in simulate.test.ts including one with pre-existing non-baseline state in the touched dimension
UNQUANTIFIED (typed sentinel, exported const) is a distinct value from $0 for any lever with no signal in the current data — never report 0 for 'not measured'

Integer micro-cents everywhere; floor exactly once at the end of costOfEvent's gross computation, never per token category; cents conversion (half-up) happens exactly once at the report boundary via microCentsToCents

One pricing function: costOfEvent() in src/pricing.ts is the only place tokens*rate is computed; simulate.ts calls it via a synthetic never-emitted UsageEvent — a lever must never re-derive the formula

Levers compound (multiply) by default; may only be summed when provably disjoint token classes, and that disjointness is pinned by a test (acceptance.test.ts) designed to fail the instant a new finding lever name appears, forcing a deliberate choice to extend the sum or switch to compounding
No routing lever, ever — a different model answering is a different answer and fails the identity guarantee; dedicated tests assert no routingCurve field and no routing-shaped assumption keys exist

Headline savings figure (savings.allMeasured) can never be smaller than any individual finding it claims to contain — a property test over arbitrary traffic, the regression test for the shipped $0.00-over-$374.93 bug

Every event-skip/exclusion reason (unknown_model, unknown_tier, malformed, and any new lever-specific exclusion) must produce a warning; a report or CLI run that silently empties a denominator to 0 must refuse (exit 1) rather than print a confident $0.00
No new dependency, no network egress from src/detect/ or src/simulate.ts — importer/lever purity is tested by stubbing fetch to throw
Determinism: identical input must produce byte-identical / JSON-identical report and HTML output across repeated runs — no clock, no Math.random, no unguarded object-iteration order
Customer-supplied strings reaching auditHtml.ts (lever detail/evidence text, model names, workspace ids) must be passed through esc(); dedicated XSS test exists

A lever's evidence claim should map to one of the five existing EvidenceClass values (PASS_ABSOLUTE/PASS_METADATA/PASS_SCHEDULING/PASS_REPLAY/CONTRACTUAL_ONLY) from src/evidence.ts rather than inventing a new tag ad hoc

Every counter a lever adds to a shared object mutated across multiple call sites in cli.ts (provenance-shaped objects) must be listed at BOTH the initializer literal and the accumulation merge loop, or it silently reads as undefined downstream — cliContract.test.ts greps cli.ts's source for every key by name to catch this
testPatterns: Hand-computed-by-a-different-instrument fixtures: every dollar/token figure in a test is asserted against a value computed by hand in an inline comment, never against the code's own output (spec §10's explicit rule) — e.g. simulate.test.ts's '100 MTok input... -> $750.00 baseline' and ttlRightSizing.test.ts's 'opus-5: 1h write 1000, 5m write 625 -> 375 recoverable per token'

Inline UsageEvent[] literal builders (small ev()/object-literal helpers) for unit-level detector/simulate tests, NOT fixtures/*.jsonl — fixtures/mixed.jsonl, dupes.jsonl, malformed.jsonl, cache-ttl.jsonl, nokey.jsonl, compaction.jsonl are reserved for importer-level and end-to-end report/auditHtml tests that need the full import path

Paired negative+positive controls: every 'X triggers a warning/finding' test is immediately followed by a 'clean traffic does NOT trigger it' control test in the same file, so a broken condition (always-true or always-false) cannot pass silently

Regression tests documented as prose-then-property: a comment names the bug, the date found, and who found it (usually 'an adversarial review'), then the test asserts a general property that happens to cover the reported case — not a narrow re-check of the literal reported scenario — so a future bug of the same shape fails the same test

End-to-end subprocess tests via Bun.spawn(['bun','run', CLI, ...]) asserting on real exit codes and stderr text for CLI-boundary contracts (flag validation, missing-value errors, empty-report refusal) — not just calling the exported TS functions directly

Source-text-grep cross-checks: reading a source file's raw text (cli.ts, README.md, RUNNING.md, site pages) with readFileSync/regex and diffing it against a runtime-derived list of truth (Object.keys of a live object, the register's loaded entries, an actual child-process test-count run) to catch 'two places that must agree but don't' — used at both function scope (cliContract.test.ts) and repo scope (publishedTestCount.test.ts, publishedRates.test.ts, publishedCounts.test.ts)
Determinism tests: JSON.stringify(report) or renderAuditHtml(report) called twice on identical input and asserted byte-identical

Property-over-fixture tests for headline-vs-findings arithmetic (acceptance.test.ts): iterate r.findings and assert an invariant holds for whatever the fixture produced, rather than asserting one hardcoded total

No mocking framework, no snapshot/golden-image testing library, no property-based testing library (fast-check etc.) anywhere in the suite — bun:test's expect()/test() only; visual/screenshot drift is checked by separate manual .mjs scripts (site/tools/shoot-audit.mjs, site/tools/page-checks.mjs, bench/margin-model.ts) run via package.json scripts, outside `bun run test`
